[Jun 18](/dotenvx/status/2067634079546397139)

This is a great time to revisit our whitepaper. There is a good solution to this problem and it is not traditional secrets managers which still have a single attack vector. You need to split the attack vector. [dotenvx.com/whitepaper.pdf](https://dotenvx.com/whitepaper.pdf) David here knows.

[](https://x.com/Davidid0x)

[David](https://x.com/Davidid0x)

[@Davidid0x](https://x.com/Davidid0x)

[Jun 17](/Davidid0x/status/2067393630738981112)

Replying to [@STP48315](https://x.com/STP48315) [@GreatGoban](https://x.com/GreatGoban) and [@cyber_rekk](https://x.com/cyber_rekk)

You should be using dotenvx to encrypt your .env files so even if this happens AND it gets past your pre-commit hooks (which I assume you have) AND it gets past your secret scanning GitHub action (which I assume you have) it’s still of very little use to an attacker.
